The Hades underworld sequence in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey (2026) was filmed practically on the black sand beaches of Hjörleifshöfði, Iceland, without the use of CGI or green screens. The scene relied on the eerie, un-fading natural daylight of the midnight sun rather than traditional nighttime lighting. Nolan chose the remote, freezing terrain because its bleak and otherworldly look contrasted sharply with Odysseus's warm Mediterranean world. This marked Nolan's third time filming in Iceland, following Batman Begins (2005) and Interstellar.

Christopher Nolan's historical epic The Odyssey (2026) is returning to more than 1,000 theaters across the U.S. and Canada on December 11, 2026, in IMAX and IMAX 70mm formats for an awards-season run.

An absolute masterpiece, but do you think The Odyssey lived up to the hype?
